entity.summary: Seychelles-registered centralized cryptocurrency exchange founded in 2018 and continuing globally. Bitget announced a phased exit from Japan in August 2026; on September 24 it confirmed unauthorized transfers affecting portions of its hot and warm wallet layers and temporarily suspended withdrawals during a security review.
entity.notes: On 2026-09-24 at 18:31 UTC, Bitget said its security systems detected unauthorized transfers affecting a limited portion of its hot and warm wallet layers. An initial estimate of approximately USD 351.6 million was later revised to approximately USD 387.5 million after additional affected assets on Zcash and TRON were classified; Bitget said the revision did not reflect additional unauthorized transfers. Bitget said cold wallets remained secure, the incident had been contained, and no further unauthorized transfers were possible. Confirmed affected assets span Ethereum and multiple EVM networks, XRP Ledger, Zcash, and TRON and include XRP, ETH, USDT, ZEC, USDC, USDT0, XAUt, BNB, AVAX, and TRX. Withdrawals remain temporarily suspended while additional security checks and remediation continue. Bitget said a withdrawal plan would be announced by 2026-09-26 04:00 UTC and that investigations with Mandiant and SlowMist were ongoing. HEI uses limited while withdrawals are paused; do not mark dead or insolvent. Earlier third-party reports describing a cold-wallet compromise and roughly USD 170-183 million of outflows were superseded by Bitget's later first-party confirmation.

expected.summary: Seychelles-registered centralized cryptocurrency exchange founded in 2018 and continuing globally; in August 2026 Bitget announced a phased cessation of services for residents of Japan.
expected.notes: Official company material and an independent exchange profile support the 2018 founding year and continuing global operation. In March 2023, Bitget announced that BitKeep had joined the wider Bitget ecosystem; BitKeep later rebranded as Bitget Wallet. On 2026-08-03, Bitget announced a phased cessation of services for residents of Japan. This regional withdrawal does not change the exchange's global active status.

events.title: Bitget began operating
events.description: Bitget began operating as a centralized cryptocurrency exchange in 2018.
events.notes: Year-level launch marker based on official company history.

events.title: BitKeep joined the Bitget ecosystem
events.description: Bitget announced a strategic transaction that brought BitKeep into the wider Bitget ecosystem.
events.notes: BitKeep later rebranded as Bitget Wallet. The event did not change the active status of the Bitget exchange.

events.title: Bitget announced the end of services for residents of Japan
events.description: Bitget announced that it would cease serving residents of Japan, stop new registrations after 2026-08-03, place affected accounts in close-only mode from 2026-11-01, and forcibly close remaining positions from 2026-12-31 while keeping withdrawals available.
events.notes: This is a regional service withdrawal for residents of Japan. It does not establish a global shutdown or change Bitget's entity status from active.

events.title: Bitget confirmed unauthorized transfers from hot and warm wallet layers
events.description: Bitget said its security systems detected unauthorized transfers at 18:31 UTC affecting a limited portion of its hot and warm wallet layers. The exchange later revised the affected amount from approximately USD 351.6 million to approximately USD 387.5 million after classifying additional affected assets on Zcash and TRON, while stating that no additional unauthorized transfers had occurred.
events.notes: Bitget said the incident was contained and no further unauthorized transfers were possible. Confirmed affected assets span Ethereum and multiple EVM networks, XRP Ledger, Zcash, and TRON and include XRP, ETH, USDT, ZEC, USDC, USDT0, XAUt, BNB, AVAX, and TRX. Investigation and tracing with Mandiant and SlowMist remain ongoing. The attack vector and final forensic loss figure have not yet been published.

events.title: Bitget temporarily suspended withdrawals pending security review
events.description: Bitget temporarily paused withdrawals as a precaution while reviewing the wallet security incident. The exchange later said withdrawals remained suspended while additional security checks and remediation continued and that a withdrawal plan would be announced by September 26 at 04:00 UTC.
events.notes: This remains a platform-wide temporary withdrawal suspension tied to the September 24 wallet incident. The September 25 update announced a timetable for the withdrawal plan, not a confirmed restoration time. HEI should return the entity to active only after withdrawal restoration is confirmed.

evidence.title: Bitget Hot Wallet Incident — September 24, 2026
evidence.notes: First-party security notice states that unauthorized transfers were detected at 18:31 UTC, estimates approximately USD 351.6 million affected, says the breach was limited to portions of hot and warm wallet layers, says cold wallets remained secure, states the User Protection Fund held more than USD 464 million and covered the loss, confirms a temporary withdrawal suspension while deposits/trading stayed operational, and promises a full incident report with root-cause analysis and corrective actions within 24 hours.

evidence.title: Bitget confirms $351M security breach, suspends withdrawals
evidence.notes: Independent report reflecting Bitget's later confirmation of approximately USD 351.6 million affected and the hot/warm-wallet scope.

evidence.title: Nearly $352M Moved From Crypto Exchange Bitget Wallets in Suspected Hack
evidence.notes: Independent coverage quoting Bitget's CEO and reporting that withdrawals were temporarily paused while deposits and trading remained operational.

evidence.title: Bitget acknowledges $351.6M outflow incident and temporarily suspends withdrawals
evidence.notes: Independent report summarizing Bitget's first-party notice, including the temporary withdrawal suspension and continued deposit/trading availability.

evidence.title: Important updates on the September 24 Bitget security incident
evidence.notes: First-party update revises the affected amount to approximately USD 387.5 million after adding affected Zcash and TRON assets, says the revision does not represent additional unauthorized transfers, states that the incident is contained with no further unauthorized transfers possible, identifies affected networks/assets, names Mandiant and SlowMist as investigation partners, confirms withdrawals remain suspended, and says a withdrawal plan will be announced by 2026-09-26 04:00 UTC.
